successCriteria.description: `src/shared/types/index.ts` exists and exports three canonical enums: `LeaveType` (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY), `LeaveRequestStatus` (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED), and `LeaveBalanceStatus` (ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, EXPIRED).

`src/shared/error-types.ts` exists and exports five error classes: abstract `AppError` (extends Error, has `statusCode: number` and `code: string`), `NotFoundError` (404), `ValidationError` (400, carries `details: unknown[]`), `ConflictError` (409), and `UnauthorizedError` (401).

`src/shared/base-repository.ts` exists and exports a generic abstract class `BaseRepository<T>` with: constructor taking a Knex instance, abstract `tableName: string`, and methods `findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>`, `findAll(filter?: Partial<T>): Promise<T[]>`, `create(data: Partial<T>): Promise<T>`, `update(id: string, data: Partial<T>): Promise<T | null>`, `delete(id: string): Promise<boolean>`.

Jest unit tests exist in `tests/unit/shared/` covering error-types (instantiation, status codes, inheritance chains) and base-repository (method signatures, abstract enforcement, Knex integration). All tests pass.
TypeScript compilation succeeds with strict mode (no implicit any, strict null checks) — `tsc --noEmit` passes.

constraints: BaseRepository constructor must accept a Knex instance (imported from 'knex'), not a pg Pool — per the intent's explicit instruction and HARNESS.json stack description.

All error classes must follow the inheritance chain: AppError (abstract) → NotFoundError / ValidationError / ConflictError / UnauthorizedError. AppError must be abstract and not directly instantiable.
Enums must use TypeScript string enums (not const enums or union types) to ensure runtime values exist for downstream consumers.
No `any` type usage — use `unknown` with type guards per HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`.
This phase has zero dependencies on any other phase files — it is the foundation all other phases build upon.
outOfScope: Additional LeaveType values beyond ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY (UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY mentioned in ARCHITECTURE.md reconciliation table are deferred to later phases).
Additional LeaveBalanceStatus values beyond ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, EXPIRED (FROZEN, CLOSED mentioned in ARCHITECTURE.md lifecycle states are deferred).
Database migrations, table DDL, Knex migration files, or knexfile configuration — these are Phase 8.
Any module-level code (leave, balance, policy, employee, notification, audit-log) — these are Phases 2–10.
Fastify integration, routes, controllers, services, or middleware — these are Phases 5–7 and 10.
RBAC enforcement, audit logging, input validation at API boundaries — these are covered by later phases and golden principles, not this foundation phase.

ambiguities.description: Should `BaseRepository` methods (`findById`, `findAll`, `create`, `update`, `delete`) be abstract (forcing each subclass to implement them) or should they have default concrete implementations using the injected Knex instance? The intent lists method signatures without bodies, which could mean either approach. Default implementations would reduce duplication across Phase 2–4 repositories; abstract methods would give each module full control.
options: Abstract methods — subclasses must implement all five
Concrete default implementations using Knex — subclasses inherit and optionally override
Mixed: findById/findAll/delete have defaults; create/update are abstract

ambiguities.description: What `code` string values should each error subclass use? The intent specifies `AppError` has a `code: string` field but does not prescribe values for `NotFoundError`, `ValidationError`, `ConflictError`, or `UnauthorizedError`. Consistent codes are needed for error handling and logging across all phases.
options: Use HTTP reason phrases: 'Not Found', 'Bad Request', 'Conflict', 'Unauthorized'
